title: What If Lake Powell Hit Dead Pool?

scenes.text: What if Lake Powell dropped so low that water stopped flowing through its dam?
That level is called dead pool, about 120 feet below where the dam's turbines shut down.
Power would fail first, because below that level turbines can suck in air and be damaged.
At dead pool, no water flows downstream to Lake Mead, which supplies Nevada, Arizona and California.
The shallow reservoir would warm up, which could fuel toxic algae and push out fish.
About 40 million people rely on the Colorado River. Experts say dead pool cannot be ruled out without major cuts in water use.
